name: Accord LED Desk Aquarium (BG-29)
summary: A novelty office aquarium that combines a small tank with a pen holder, digital calendar and gooseneck LED. It runs on low voltage and has an undergravel filter.
bestFor: A desk ornament with a couple of easy plants or a few shrimp.
highlights: Pen holder and digital clock/calendar built in

specs.Voltage: AC 230/115 V (24 V to pump and light)

watchOut: The tank is only 12.8 cm tall and the pump and light are tiny, so treat it as a novelty.

name: Arts LED Aquarium (ME-175)
summary: A small framed desktop tank with a built-in filter and clip LED. Two slightly different heights, several frame colours.
bestFor: Office desks and first nano tanks with low-light plants.
watchOut: The 2 W LED is only enough for undemanding plants like mosses and Anubias.

name: BYG Series Aquarium
summary: A cylinder-look tank with a split, flip-up lid made of two half-circles, a top biological filter and built-in lighting. Two sizes, 26 and 86 litres.
bestFor: A decorative round-style tank for easy plants and small fish.

specs.Dimensions: Overall size including the hood; the litre figure is the maker's water volume

watchOut: Curved glass is harder to scape and photograph, and the 7 W and 10 W lamps only suit low-light plants.

name: Cornucopia Betta Cube (DY-150)
summary: A tiny betta cube with an LED in the lid, offered in several pastel colours. It is about 20 cm on each side, so very small.
bestFor: A single betta on a desk, with a few easy plants.

specs.Colours: Green, orange-red, pink, yellow, black, white

watchOut: Very small water volume means temperature and water quality swing quickly, and no filter is listed.

name: DY Series Tabletop Tank
summary: Small tabletop tanks with the pump in the base, so water and electrics are kept apart, plus a multi-stage bottom filter and surface skimmer. Round and rectangular shapes, with or without A styling.
bestFor: A betta or a few shrimp on a desk.
highlights: Motor sits in the base, separated from the water
Flow valve to cut water noise
watchOut: Very small volume, so it needs regular small water changes.

name: E Series Cabinet Aquarium (EAF / EAZ / EAM / EDM / EHM / ELM)
summary: An open-top-look cabinet aquarium with a partitioned sump-style filter in the base, LED tubes and a wireless touch-screen controller. Boyu sells the same tank under six series codes that differ only in cabinet and trim styling.
bestFor: Large community or planted displays where you want filtration and lighting built into the furniture.
highlights: Feeding hatch that takes an auto feeder
Titanium-gold trim (EAF, EAZ) or wood-finish cabinets (EAM, EDM, EHM, ELM)

specs.Series codes: EAF, EAZ, EAM, EDM, EHM, ELM (P and D suffixes on some)

watchOut: The included LED tubes (2 x 15 to 2 x 20 W) are well short of what a demanding planted tank needs.

name: FG Series Aquarium
summary: Simple glass tanks with a separate LED unit and an optional hang-on waterfall filter. Three sizes from 41 to 62 cm long.
bestFor: A basic glass tank for a budget planted or community setup.
watchOut: Filter is optional and specs beyond dimensions are not given.

name: FY-10 Aquarium
summary: A clean, rimless-look glass tank with a lift-off lid carrying a detachable LED and an internal filter box. Designed to look good viewed from above as well as the front.
bestFor: A starter planted or shrimp tank that looks neater than most kit tanks.
highlights: Detachable LED on a removable lid
watchOut: Boyu does not publish volume, flow or light wattage.

name: Happy Family Aquarium
summary: A rounded all-in-one tank with filtration hidden in the hood and back. The fuller versions come loaded with a protein skimmer, UV, heater and night LED; the B versions keep it to pump, media and light, which is what a freshwater keeper needs.
bestFor: Someone wanting a complete, ready-to-go medium tank without piecing together equipment.
highlights: A versions add heater, UV and protein skimmer
watchOut: The skimmer on the A models is pointless in fresh water, and the HS-60 standard model uses a 150 W halogen lamp.

name: HG Series Aquarium
summary: A glossy, colourful lidded tank with a top biological filter, digital clock, water temperature readout and a touch-controlled LED. Three sizes from 32 to 80 cm long, in seven colours.
bestFor: A bright, family-friendly tank with easy plants.

specs.Colours: White, black, orange, green, yellow, red, pink

watchOut: Light output is low for the size, especially on the HG-800 (2 x 10 W).

name: LA Yayue Aquarium
summary: An aluminium-framed tank and cabinet aimed at arowana keepers, with cabinet filtration, a touch panel and remote. Narrow at 36 cm front to back.
bestFor: Tall display tanks for large fish in a narrow space.
highlights: Aluminium frame in silver, drawbench gold or drawbench black
watchOut: Only 36 cm deep, which limits aquascaping depth, and the lighting is modest.

name: LB Yapin Aquarium
summary: Boyu's bigger arowana-style tank and cabinet, with stronger cabinet filtration than the LA and LK and three LED tubes. Standard 48 cm deep or wider 60 cm L versions.
bestFor: Large fish displays or a big community tank.
watchOut: Lighting is modest for a planted setup of this size, and the maker's table labels the widest model inconsistently.

name: LE Yahuan Aquarium
summary: A tall, dark arowana-style display tank on a cabinet with a filtration system in the base, touch panel and remote. Seven sizes, including wider L versions.
bestFor: Big fish displays, or a large planted tank if you replace the lighting.
watchOut: Boyu does not publish dimensions or specs for this series, so check with a dealer.

name: LH Overlord Aquarium
summary: A deeper take on the LZ, with bent front glass, a top filter and hood LEDs, on a matching cabinet. From 85 cm up to 2.8 m.
bestFor: Big community or cichlid displays that suit extra depth.
highlights: Deeper tanks than the LZ (50 to 67 cm front to back)

specs.Colours: Snowy white, birch, cherry, mahogany, black
specs.Dimensions: Overall size including the hood; the litre figure is the maker's water volume

watchOut: A single 1,200 L/h pump across the whole range is underpowered for the larger tanks.

name: LJ Series Aquarium
summary: Hexagonal-fronted tanks with a flip-up ABS hood, top biological filter and tube lighting. Three sizes from 22 to 68 litres. Boyu lists these on its Chinese pages only.
bestFor: A compact display tank for a few fish and easy plants.

specs.Dimensions: Overall size including the hood; the litre figure is the maker's water volume

watchOut: The lighting is energy-saving tube based rather than modern LED.

name: LK Series Aquarium
summary: A slim black or white tank and cabinet with filtration in the base. The A versions get a stronger pump.
bestFor: A medium display for a hallway or narrow room.
watchOut: Only 32 cm deep, and a single 10 to 16 W LED is weak for plants.

name: LZ Modern Aquarium
summary: A large curved-front tank on a cabinet with a top filter and LED lighting in the hood. The single piece of bent front glass gives an uninterrupted view. A big range from 84 cm to 3 m.
bestFor: Large community displays where a seamless front matters more than aquascaping flexibility.
highlights: Bent front glass, no corner seams

specs.Colours: Snowy white, birch, cherry, mahogany, black
specs.Dimensions: Overall size including the hood; the litre figure is the maker's water volume

watchOut: Every size uses the same 1,200 L/h pump, which is weak on the bigger tanks, and the hood limits lighting upgrades.

name: Magic LED Aquarium (ME-213 / ME-270)
summary: A compact cube tank with a lid-mounted multi-mode LED and touch controls, running on 12 V. The ME-270H and 270RH are taller, with an external filter; the RH adds ultra-clear glass and an IR remote.
bestFor: A tidy nano on a desk or shelf with easy plants.
highlights: Feeding and ventilation holes in the lid
ME-270RH: ultra-clear glass and IR remote
watchOut: The lid covers the top fully, which limits emersed growth and plant choice.

name: MEZ Intelligent Aquarium
summary: A tall, lidded nano with a multi-mode LED whose brightness and colour you can adjust. The A versions use touch control; the standard versions add app control with a 24-hour natural light cycle. It runs an external filter.
bestFor: A compact planted or community tank with some lighting control built in.
highlights: Adjustable brightness and colour, app control on non-A models
watchOut: Tall, narrow tanks are harder to light well at the bottom and to aquascape.

name: Mia LED Aquarium (DSN-315)
summary: A small curved-lid desktop tank with a submersible filter and LED. About 32 cm long.
bestFor: A simple starter nano.
watchOut: The 0.6 W LED is a display light; plants beyond mosses and Anubias will struggle.

name: MS Series Aquarium
summary: A tidy lidded nano range with a top biological filter and a touch-controlled multi-mode LED. Three sizes from 20 to 45 litres.
bestFor: Beginners wanting a complete small tank for easy plants, shrimp or a betta.
watchOut: Low light output (5 to 7 W) suits low-light plants only.

name: MT Mini Aquarium
summary: A curved-front kit tank with an internal biological filter, LED tubes and small cooling fans in the hood. Three sizes from 25 to 80 litres.
bestFor: Beginners after a complete kit for easy plants and small fish.
highlights: Internal bio filter with sponge, balls, carbon and ceramic
LED tubes plus 12 V hood fans

specs.Dimensions: Overall size including the hood; the litre figure is the maker's water volume

watchOut: The curved front distorts the view and makes aquascaping harder.

name: Refinement Aquarium (JDG-270)
summary: A small cube tank with a coloured frame, a swivelling lamp arm and built-in filtration. It ships with a 9 W energy-saving lamp, though Boyu says LED options exist.
bestFor: A beginner nano cube for easy plants.

specs.Colours: Pink, orange, aqua blue, grey, black

watchOut: The standard 9 W compact fluorescent lamp is dated and will need replacing sooner than an LED.

name: XF Suspension Aquarium
summary: An 80 cm tank on a matching cabinet with a multi-stage bottom filter, surface skimmer and a flow valve to keep the water noise down. The JE version is taller.
bestFor: A medium planted or community display with everything included.
highlights: Multi-stage bottom filter with surface skimmer
watchOut: The 18 W light is only enough for low to medium light plants.

name: ZDT Classic Aquarium
summary: A traditional curved-front aquarium and cabinet set with lighting in the hood and a choice of filter systems. Boyu pitches the red and blue LED mix as plant and colour friendly. Sizes from about 80 cm to 1.5 m.
bestFor: A classic furniture-style community tank for the living room.
highlights: Red and blue enhanced LED lighting, some models add an 11 W PL tube
Several filter options in the range

specs.Colours: Birch, black, snowy white, cherry, mahogany
specs.Variants: A4 / B4 versions have 4 LED tubes and no listed pump
specs.Dimensions: Overall size including the hood; the litre figure is the maker's water volume

watchOut: Hood lighting is modest and hard to upgrade; the A4 and B4 variants come without a listed pump.

name: ZJ Series Aquarium
summary: Curved-front lidded tanks with an internal pump feeding a top filter and a lid LED. Sizes from 20 to 84 litres; the A versions are taller.
bestFor: Beginners after a complete medium kit tank.
highlights: Top filter fed by an internal pump
watchOut: Lighting is weak for the size (6 to 10 W).

name: BT Mini Tank
summary: Two tiny desktop all-in-ones of about 5 litres, one squared off (BT-111) and one round (BT-112). Each has a small internal filter with a replaceable cartridge and a 2 W white LED running off a 12 V transformer.
bestFor: A moss, Anubias or shrimp display on a desk where you want everything in one box.
highlights: Around 5 litres, built for desks and shelves
watchOut: At around 5 litres this is too small for most fish, a betta included, and the light is only good for low-light plants.

name: GT3000 Series Glass Tank
summary: Plain frameless glass tanks in five sizes from about 15 to 57 litres, offered with either bent-glass round front corners or square corners with black silicone. They are sold bare, which is exactly what many scapers want as a starting point.
bestFor: A budget nano or small scape where you plan to choose your own light, filter and CO2.
highlights: Five sizes from 30 to 50 cm long
4 mm glass on the two smallest, 5 mm on the rest
Nested value sets of 3 or 5 tanks available

specs.Corners: Round (bent glass) or square with black silicone

watchOut: Glass is on the thin side for the 45 and 50 cm sizes, so sit them on a levelling mat on a flat, solid surface; no lid, light or filter is included.

name: GT6000 Cube Glass Tank
summary: A 25 cm glass cube in two heights, 15 and 18 litres, with silver or black silicone. It is a simple, cheap way into a nano cube scape.
bestFor: A shrimp or nano cube with mosses, small epiphytes and a carpet, where the taller GT-6002 gives a little more room for stem plants.
highlights: 25 x 25 cm footprint, 25 or 30 cm tall
watchOut: Cubes this small swing in temperature and water chemistry quickly, so they need steady maintenance.

name: GTR Curved Glass Tank Kit
summary: A curved-front glass tank sold as a full kit on a matching black cabinet, with a lid, LED lighting and a top filter box driven by a powerhead. Three footprints from 27 to 81 litres, all at the same 76 cm cabinet height.
bestFor: Someone who wants a complete tank-and-stand package for a low-tech planted community tank without piecing parts together.
highlights: Curved front glass on a matching cabinet
Lid with white and blue LEDs on a 3-way touch switch
Top filter box and powerhead included

specs.Included: Cabinet, lid, white/blue LED light, top filter box with powerhead

watchOut: The curved front bends the view slightly and is awkward to scrape, and the included lid light and top filter are basic, so a serious planted tank will need upgrades.

name: aquafamily
summary: aquafamily is a 66 litre starter set with a lid-mounted RGBW LED you can program over WiFi, plus a corner filter, a preset heater and a thermometer. The app guides families through feeding and maintenance.
bestFor: A first aquarium for a family, or a tidy low-tech planted tank on a sturdy sideboard.
highlights: RGBW LED with sunrise, sunset, clouds and moonlight, set via app or browser
Comes with aqua 160 corner filter and 100 W thermopreset heater
Polished glass edges and a base frame
App reminders for feeding, water changes and filter cleaning

specs.Includes: LED lid, aqua 160 filter, thermopreset 100 W heater, thermometer

watchOut: The lid light is aimed at general viewing, so demanding carpeting plants will struggle without extra light.

name: vivaline LED
summary: vivaline LED is a complete aquarium and cabinet set with a lid, LED light, Biopower internal filter and heater. A swappable decorative panel on the cabinet lets you change the look to match your room.
bestFor: Low-tech community planted tanks where you want everything matched and ready to set up.
highlights: Tank, cabinet, LED lid, filter and heater all included
126 L comes with a Biopower 160, 180 L with a Biopower 200
Cabinet front panel can be swapped even with the tank full
Pine, oak grey, white or anthracite finishes
watchOut: The single 13 or 17 W LED is fine for easy plants, but a stem-heavy or carpeted scape will want a stronger light and a canister.

name: Lido LED
summary: A taller, deeper take on the Rio, with a near-cube footprint that gives you more front-to-back room for layering plants and hardscape. Like the rest of the Juwel range it arrives with a Bioflow internal filter, AquaHeat heater and MultiLux LED lid. The extra height looks great but makes light reach the substrate a bit harder.
bestFor: Anyone with limited wall length who still wants depth for a layered scape or taller stem plants.
highlights: Two sizes, 120 and 200 litres, with a deep, tall footprint
Bioflow M internal filter and AquaHeat heater fitted in the rear corner
MultiLux LED lighting in the lid, upgradeable to HeliaLux Spectrum
Optional matching cabinet in black, white, grey or light wood

specs.Included: Bioflow M internal filter, AquaHeat heater, MultiLux LED lighting
specs.Cabinet: Optional matching cabinet (73 cm tall for 120, 80 cm for 200)

watchOut: At 58 to 65 cm tall, the stock light struggles to grow demanding foreground plants at the bottom.

name: Primo LED
summary: Juwel's entry-level 60 cm tank, with a lid, LED light, small internal filter and heater all included. It sits on a built-in safety base frame, so it goes straight onto a sturdy surface without a mat. A sensible first planted tank for easy species, though the single small LED limits what you can grow.
bestFor: Beginners wanting a complete 60 cm tank for low-light plants, shrimp or a small community.
highlights: Two heights on the same 61 x 31 cm footprint: 57 and 70 litres
Bioflow One internal filter with 300 L/h pump and AquaHeat 50 W heater hidden in the filter
NovoLux LED 60 light (8 W); the lid takes up to three units
Feeding hatch in the lid works with automatic feeders

specs.Included: Bioflow One filter with Eccoflow 300 pump (4.4 W), AquaHeat 50 W heater, NovoLux LED 60 (8 W)

watchOut: One 8 W NovoLux is only enough for undemanding plants such as Anubias, ferns and Cryptocoryne.

name: Rio LED
summary: Juwel's classic rectangular tank, sold with the filter, heater and lighting already fitted. Every size comes with a Bioflow internal filter tucked into a rear corner, an AquaHeat heater inside that filter and a MultiLux LED unit in the lid. It is a framed, lidded tank, so it suits community planted tanks more than open, rimless aquascapes.
bestFor: Keepers who want a complete, matched setup in one box and are happy with a lidded, framed look.
highlights: Six sizes from 125 to 450 litres, all with filter, heater and light included
Bioflow internal filter sits in the back corner, so there are no hoses or canister to house
MultiLux LED lid with two replaceable tubes; HeliaLux Spectrum is a direct upgrade
Matching cabinet available for every size in black, white, grey or light wood

specs.Included: Bioflow internal filter, AquaHeat heater, MultiLux LED lighting
specs.Cabinet: Optional matching cabinet (73 cm tall for 125/180/240, 80 cm for 290/350/450)

watchOut: The stock two-tube MultiLux suits easy plants; a demanding carpet in the deeper sizes will want a stronger light and CO2.

name: Trigon LED
summary: A corner aquarium with a curved front, designed to tuck into the corner of a room and still show off a lot of water. It ships with a matching corner cabinet, a Bioflow internal filter, AquaHeat heater and MultiLux LED lighting. The triangular footprint gives real depth, but it is an awkward shape for a classic aquascape layout.
bestFor: Rooms where a corner is the only spot for a sizeable tank and you want a complete, matched set.
highlights: Corner shape makes use of space most tanks cannot
Supplied with matching corner cabinet, Bioflow filter, heater and MultiLux LED
Depth of 70 to 87 cm gives a strong sense of perspective

specs.Included: Matching corner cabinet (73 cm tall), Bioflow internal filter, AquaHeat heater, MultiLux LED lighting

extra.Lighting: MultiLux LED (12 W and 23 W tubes)

watchOut: Deep water and a wide triangular lid make even lighting and reaching the back for planting and trimming harder.

name: Vio Cube
summary: A compact 54 litre cube from Juwel that comes ready to run with filter, heater and LED lighting. The cube shape suits an iwagumi or a small jungle scape viewed from the front, and it fits on a desk or sideboard. A matching SBX cabinet is sold separately if you want it at viewing height.
bestFor: Small-space keepers wanting a tidy, complete nano setup for shrimp, small fish and easy plants.
highlights: 54 litres in a 41 x 36 x 47 cm cube with 5 mm glass
Bioflow S filter with a 300 L/h Eccoflow pump and AquaHeat 50 W heater included
NovoLux LED 40 Neo lighting in the cover, with a feeding opening
Built-in base frame, so no separate mat is needed

specs.Included: Bioflow S filter with Eccoflow 300 pump (4.4 W), AquaHeat 50 W heater, NovoLux LED 40 Neo
specs.Cabinet: Optional Vio Cube SBX cabinet (73 cm tall)

watchOut: The lidded design and small included light suit low-tech planting rather than a high-light CO2 scape.

name: Vision LED
summary: Juwel's bow-front tank, where a curved front pane gives the scape a wider, more immersive look from the sofa. It comes as a set with a matching cabinet, plus the usual Bioflow internal filter, AquaHeat heater and MultiLux LED lighting. The curve adds drama but also some distortion when you view from an angle.
bestFor: Living-room display tanks where the tank is a feature piece and you like the bow-front look.
highlights: Curved front glass for a panoramic view of the layout
Supplied with matching cabinet, Bioflow filter, heater and MultiLux LED
Deeper 46 to 61 cm footprint on the larger models leaves room for layering

specs.Included: Matching cabinet (73 cm tall), Bioflow internal filter, AquaHeat heater, MultiLux LED lighting

watchOut: Curved glass bends the view at the edges, which some aquascapers find distracting for photos.

name: HighLine Optiwhite
summary: Oase's large furniture-style aquarium sets, pairing a low-iron Optiwhite tank with a flush, handle-free cabinet. Unlike the Juwel sets, lighting and filtration are not included: you choose your own lights and an external filter, which sits on a pull-out shelf inside the cabinet. That makes it a good blank canvas for a serious planted tank, at a serious price.
bestFor: Keepers planning a large, long-term display who want to pick their own canister filter and lights.
highlights: Optiwhite glass for a clear view without the green tint
Four sizes from 202 to 580 litres, 10 to 12 mm glass
Pull-out cabinet shelf and dry duct for an external filter and tidy cables
Removable aluminium lid with feeding flap; lighting chosen separately

specs.Included: Aquarium, base cabinet and connections; no light, filter or heater
specs.Lighting: Sold separately (Oase Classic LED or Premium LED)
specs.Cabinet: Push-to-open doors, adjustable feet, pull-out filter shelf, optional drawers

watchOut: The price covers only tank and cabinet; budget separately for lights, filter and heater.

name: ScaperLine
summary: A rimless, mitre-cut Optiwhite tank built for aquascaping, sold as a set with a flush matching cabinet. The cabinet is laid out for a scaper, with a pull-out shelf for an external filter, magnetic tool holders and a hidden cable port. No light or filter is included, so you build the tech around it yourself.
bestFor: Aquascapers who want an open-top, show-quality tank and cabinet that match, and already know which light and filter they want.
highlights: Rimless Optiwhite glass with hand-glued mitred edges
Cabinet has a pull-out filter shelf, magnetic tool and towel holders
Handle-free, push-to-open doors keep the lines clean

specs.Included: Aquarium and matching cabinet; no light, filter or heater
specs.Colours: Black or grey (white cabinet also offered)
specs.Cabinet: Also sold on its own (see ScaperLine Cabinet)

watchOut: Open-top tanks lose more water to evaporation and need a light that hangs or mounts on the rim.

name: StyleLine
summary: Oase's complete starter sets: tank, cabinet, BioPlus Thermo internal filter with built-in heater, and a pair of Classic LED daylight tubes. A removable glass sliding cover and aluminium trim along the bottom hide the waterline and substrate edge. It is a tidy, modern-looking all-in-one for someone who does not want to piece a system together.
bestFor: Beginners after a complete, good-looking tank and cabinet set for a low-tech planted community tank.
highlights: BioPlus Thermo corner filter with integrated heater included
Two Classic LED daylight (6,500 K) tubes supplied

specs.Included: Aquarium, cabinet, BioPlus Thermo internal filter, 2 x Classic LED daylight

watchOut: The two daylight tubes are enough for easy plants, but a high-light setup would need a lighting upgrade.

name: AT Series View Aquarium
summary: Desktop tanks with an integrated filter and eight-colour gradient LED, from 17 to 55 litres. B and C versions differ in style.
bestFor: A decorative fish tank on a desk or counter.
watchOut: The colour-cycling light is for show; plants will want a steady white light.

name: H2FU Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet tank with a U-shaped baffle in the sump and a partition screen design, from 1 m to 2 m long. Five depth and size bands cover 191 to 922 litres.
bestFor: Fish keepers wanting a mid-to-large sump tank with plenty of sizing choice.

extra.Filtration: Large four-way bottom filter + U baffle
Large four-way bottom filter + U baffle
Large four-way bottom filter + U baffle
Large four-way bottom filter + U baffle
Large four-way bottom filter + U baffle

watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: H2G Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: SunSun's giant display range, from 1.8 m up to a 3 m long, 1,350 litre tank with a large sump and DC pump. Two depths, 61 and 74 cm.
bestFor: Very large fish displays in homes or offices.
highlights: Remote control and large touch screen
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: H2TS Series Filter Aquarium
summary: A lidded cabinet tank that pairs a sump with an efficient JTP frequency pump on most sizes. It comes in three depths from 42 to 60 cm.
bestFor: Keepers wanting a big sump tank with lower running costs on the pump.
highlights: Low-power JTP pumps (18 to 25 W) on most models
Aluminium lifting lid and touch display

specs.Colours: Yellow rosewood, red rosewood, gold wood grain, black

watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: H3TS Series Barrel Filter Aquarium
summary: Instead of a sump, this cabinet tank runs its filtration through closed barrel-style filter buckets hidden in the stand, fed by an STP-3800 pump. A sealed setup like this loses less CO2 than a trickle sump, which matters if you plan to inject.
bestFor: Keepers who want a cabinet tank with sealed filtration, including CO2-injected planted setups.
highlights: Closed barrel filters in the cabinet

specs.Colours: Yellow rosewood, red rosewood, gold wood grain

name: HAT Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A tall cabinet aquarium with an aluminium lifting lid, ultra-clear glass and a sump in the stand. Eight sizes in two depths, from 160 to 385 litres.
bestFor: People who want a clearer-glass sump tank without going up to the largest sizes.
highlights: Gold apple, light wood or teak finish
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HCB Rear Filter Aquarium
summary: A compact cube-ish tank on a matching stand, with the filter hidden in a rear compartment instead of a sump. It ships with an ADT spotlight on a stand, which gives it a more open, scape-friendly look than SunSun's lidded fish tanks.
bestFor: A small open-top planted or nano fish tank where you want the filter out of sight.
highlights: Rear filter chamber with HQJ-700G pump

specs.Colours: Red, blues, orange, turquoise, yellow, white

watchOut: The included ADT-110C and 120C lights are modest (10 to 20 W), so fast carpeting plants may want more light.

name: HEE Series Aluminium Frame Aquarium
summary: A large aluminium-framed tank on a matching cabinet, with a four-chamber sump hidden underneath and a DC return pump already fitted. It comes in two depths (60 and 73 cm front to back) across three lengths, so it is built for big display fish rather than a nano scape.
bestFor: Keepers planning a big community or large-fish display who want the filtration and plumbing sorted out of the box.
highlights: Six sizes from about 500 to 860 litres
Ultra-clear glass in an aluminium frame
JDP-10000 DC return pump and AQ smart controllers included
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HEK Series Open Aquarium
summary: An open, ultra-clear glass tank sold with a slim ADP light on telescopic legs and an HBL hang-on filter. The 30 to 80 cm sizes line up with common aquascaping footprints.
bestFor: A first planted nano or small scape where you want tank, light and filter in one purchase.
highlights: ADP stand light and HBL hang-on filter included
Optional matching cabinet for 300 and 380 sizes

specs.Included: ADP or ADS light, HBL hang-on filter

watchOut: The included lights are low wattage (2.5 to 8 W on the small sizes), so stick to easy, low-light plants or upgrade the light.

name: HEZ Series All-in-One Aquarium
summary: One family covering everything from a 12 litre desktop tank to a 250 litre cabinet set. Small sizes use a top filter, the 800 to 1200 models a side filter, and the D versions add a sump in the stand.
bestFor: Beginners who want a complete kit and may want to size up later within the same look.
highlights: Ultra-clear glass, 8 to 10 mm on the big models
Remote-controlled LED lighting and temperature display

specs.Filtration: Top filter (300 to 600), side filter (800 to 1200), sump (D models)
specs.Also sold as: HEW series, and HE series for the 300 to 600 sizes

watchOut: Colour-changing lid LEDs suit fish display; for demanding plants you would add a proper planted light.

name: HFC Series Open-Top Aquarium
summary: An open-top tank on a matching cabinet, designed to run with an external canister (SunSun suggests the HW-302 or HW-303A). With no lid or built-in sump, it is the most scape-friendly of SunSun's cabinet sets.
bestFor: Planted-tank keepers who want a clean open tank and stand and prefer to pick their own canister and light.
highlights: 45 cm deep, good room for a layered scape
Open top for hanging or stand lights
watchOut: No light or filter included, so budget for both.

name: HJJ Series Home Aquarium
summary: A mid-size home aquarium set with a drawer-style sump in the cabinet, LED lighting in the lid and a CQB pump. The narrow 33 cm depth keeps it easy to fit against a wall, from a 70 litre starter up to about 230 litres.
bestFor: Someone after a tidy, ready-to-run fish tank for a living room with a modest footprint.
highlights: Drawer-type four-stage bottom filter, easy to pull out and rinse
Front and rear glass flaps for feeding
Brushed silver, black or gold finish

specs.Filtration: Four-way drawer sump (1000 and 1200 add a sediment chamber)

extra.Filtration: New four-way bottom filter (drawer)+front separation sedimentation bin
New four-way bottom filter (drawer)+front separation sedimentation bin

watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HLF Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a sump and a noticeably brighter lid light than SunSun's similar HLFT range (20 to 46 W). Two depths and nine lengths from 60 to 150 cm.
bestFor: Fish keepers who want a sump tank with a bit more light for easy plants.
highlights: Nine sizes from 90 to about 335 litres
Brighter LED lid lights than HLFT
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HLFT Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A broad cabinet-aquarium range with a sump below, offered in four depths from 35 to 60 cm. It keeps the same basic layout across 16 sizes, so it is easy to pick one to fit a specific wall.
bestFor: Fish keepers after a standard sump tank in a size that matches their space.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HMT Series Home Aquarium
summary: A tall, lidded cabinet aquarium with a sump and AQ smart controllers, sold in two depths from 60 to 150 cm. It is SunSun's everyday family-tank layout.
bestFor: Households wanting a complete fish tank that looks like furniture.
highlights: AQ-192H lid and AQ-130 cabinet controllers
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HMTX Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet tank with a sump, clear front and back glass and extra-clear side panels. It runs from 60 to 150 cm in two depths, with an HJ-2200 return pump across the range.
bestFor: A family tank where you want the filter and plumbing inside the cabinet.

specs.Glass: Clear front and back, ultra-clear sides

watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HNE-380 Desktop Aquarium
summary: A 26 litre white desktop tank with twin 3 W colour-changing LEDs and an HQJ-500G pump. It runs on a 12 V adapter.
bestFor: A simple desk tank for small fish.
watchOut: SunSun gives no dimensions for this model, and the pump must stay submerged.

name: HR Series Desktop Aquarium
summary: Small HD glass desktop tanks with a rain-shower filter and flip-up feeding hatch, from 6 to 52 litres. White or black trim.
bestFor: A tidy starter tank for small fish.

name: HRG Series Desktop Aquarium
summary: A range of curved-corner desktop tanks with a lid light and pump, from 29 to 80 cm long. The larger sizes are really small floor tanks without a cabinet.
bestFor: Beginners who want a complete small tank.
highlights: Five sizes from 29 to 80 cm long
Single flat front, curved side edges

specs.Glass: Hot-bent, flat front and curved edges

watchOut: Sizes are hand-measured and include the lid and base, and SunSun's listed volumes for most sizes do not add up against those dimensions, so work out real capacity from the glass size.

name: HRG-D Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: The cabinet version of SunSun's curved-front HRG tanks, with a small sump in the stand. It is a compact option from 50 to 100 cm long.
bestFor: Someone wanting a small sump tank with a softer, curved look.
watchOut: SunSun does not publish water volumes for this range, and dimensions are hand-measured (plus or minus 1 to 2 cm).

name: HRK Series Open Nano Aquarium
summary: Open-top ultra-clear tanks with curved (hot-bent) front corners and 5 mm glass, from a 3.5 litre pico up to 55 litres. Nothing is included, which leaves you free to choose light and filter.
bestFor: Nano scapes and shrimp tanks where you want an open top and your own choice of light and filter.
watchOut: Bent-glass corners distort the view slightly at the edges.

name: HST Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a touch-screen controller and one-touch drain, sold from 60 cm up to a 2 m, 740 litre display. Deeper models circulate water down both sides into the sump.
bestFor: Keepers wanting a larger sump tank with some convenience features.
highlights: Teak, apple, gold wood grain or white walnut

specs.Filtration: Sump (dual-side overflow on ID, FD and AD models)
specs.Colours: Congo teak, golden apple, gold wood grain, white walnut

watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HUM Series Bullet-Front Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a curved, bullet-style front glass and a sump underneath. Three lengths from 1 to 1.5 m, all 44 cm deep.
bestFor: Fish keepers who like a curved front and want a big tank without fuss.
watchOut: Curved glass distorts the view at the corners, which matters more for photographing a scape than for watching fish.

name: HWK Series View Aquarium
summary: Ultra-clear open tanks on a removable base, matched with an HBL hang-on filter and ADP light (sold as a creative package). Seven sizes from 3.5 to 55 litres.
bestFor: Nano planted tanks and shrimp setups.
highlights: Matching HBL filter and ADP light

name: HWW Series Pipeless Aquarium
summary: A big display tank where the filtration runs without visible pipes in the tank, feeding a DC pump in the cabinet. It starts at 1.5 m and runs past 900 litres.
bestFor: Large display tanks where a clean, pipe-free look matters.
highlights: No visible pipework in the display
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HYM-B Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A wood-effect cabinet aquarium with a compact sump underneath and HD glass on all four sides. Four lengths from 60 to 120 cm keep it in normal living-room territory.
bestFor: Fish keepers who want a furniture-style tank with built-in filtration.
highlights: Walnut, white or grey wood finishes

specs.Lid: Front and rear glass flip cover

watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: HYTX Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium range that mixes sump models (ED, ID, FD, AD) with IT models that use barrel filters instead. Sizes run from 1 m to 2 m.
bestFor: Keepers who want the choice between a sump and sealed barrel filtration in the same cabinet style.
highlights: IT models use sealed barrel filters

specs.Filtration: Sump (ED, ID, FD, AD) or barrel filters (IT)
specs.Colours: Wine red, BMW grey, pearl white

watchOut: Sump models trickle off injected CO2 quickly; pick an IT model if you plan to run CO2 for plants.

name: Joy Series Aquarium
summary: A cabinet tank with a small sump and a three-colour switchable LED lid. Four lengths from 80 to 150 cm, all with a CQB-2500 return pump.
bestFor: A colourful living-room fish tank where the kit is all included.
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: Stream Tank Series Aquarium
summary: A low, 45 cm tall tank on a cabinet, lit by one or two ADT-120C stand lights rather than a closed lid. The shallow height and open top make it one of SunSun's more aquascape-friendly cabinet sets.
bestFor: Planted-tank keepers who want a shallow, open-top display on a matching stand.
highlights: Shallow 45 cm tank height, easy to reach the substrate
Open top with ADT-120C stand lighting

specs.Lighting: ADT-120C stand light (two on 1000 mm models)
specs.Styles: A, B and C cabinets share the same tank sizes

watchOut: Two ADT-120C lights on the longer tanks is a low-to-medium light setup, fine for easy plants but not for high-tech carpets.

name: XHF Rear Filter Aquarium
summary: A small tank-and-stand set from SunSun's Xiaoli line with a filter chamber tucked behind the back glass. B models come with an LED light and glass flap lid; C models are the lower, lidless version.
bestFor: A neat first aquarium or bedroom tank where cables and filter should stay hidden.
highlights: Stand raised on a 10 cm bracket
watchOut: The rear chamber eats a little depth from the display area, so the scape is shallower than the outside size suggests.

name: XHM Desktop Aquarium
summary: Two very small desktop tanks with a built-in JP-230G pump and 12 V light. They suit a betta or a few shrimp.
bestFor: A single betta or small shrimp colony on a desk.
watchOut: No volume is published, and the tank must sit fully flat with the pump submerged.

name: XHR Desktop Aquarium
summary: Curved-corner HD glass desktop tanks from 13 to 76 litres, each with a top circulation filter and 12 V LED. The HRX series shares the 300 and 380 sizes.
bestFor: A beginner or kids' tank on a desk or chest of drawers.

name: ZEF Series Bottom Filter Aquarium
summary: A cabinet aquarium with a sump built into the stand, sold in three depths (35, 42 and 48 cm) and lengths from 60 cm to 2 m. The range is wide enough to find a size for most rooms, and every model comes with a lid light and CQB return pump.
bestFor: Fish keepers who want a sump tank in an exact size without building plumbing themselves.
highlights: AQ smart controllers in the lid and cabinet
Grey, blue or orange cabinet colours
watchOut: The in-cabinet sump trickles water over media, which strips injected CO2 faster than a canister, and the lid lights are aimed at showing off fish rather than growing plants.

name: ZHA Series Aluminium Arowana Aquarium
summary: A heavy-duty aluminium tank designed for arowana and other large fish, with a deep sump and DC pump on the bigger sizes. At 49 to 61 cm deep and up to 2 m long, it is a serious piece of furniture.
bestFor: Large-fish keepers who need a big, sturdy tank more than a scaping canvas.
highlights: ZZA LED bars and AQ controllers included
FD models add a sediment trap before the sump

name: ZHE Desktop Aquarium
summary: A small ultra-clear desktop tank with a built-in top filter and colour-changing LED lid, run from a 12 V adapter. Three sizes from 13 to 46 litres; J versions differ in trim.
bestFor: Nano fish or shrimp tanks on a desk.
highlights: APJ pump and top filter included

name: ZHR Desktop Aquarium
summary: A 26 litre desktop tank with curved front corners, a lid light and a small pump-driven top filter. It is a simple all-included starter size.
bestFor: A desk or bedside tank for a few small fish or shrimp.

name: 90-Degree Rimless Aquarium
summary: The budget side of the UNS range: rimless tanks with plain 90 degree joins instead of mitred corners. The glass is clear and the sizes cover common cube, nano and 45 to 60 cm footprints for noticeably less money.
bestFor: A first planted tank or a shrimp and betta setup where cost matters more than seamless corners.
highlights: Cube, nano and standard sizes from 16 cm to 60 cm
Butt-joined 90 degree corners rather than mitred edges
5 mm glass (6 mm on the 60 cm tanks)
watchOut: The glass edges are visible at the corners, which some people notice once the tank is scaped.

name: All-In-One Aquarium 30A
summary: A 30 cm rimless cube with a filter chamber built into the back behind a white panel. It hides the pump and media, so you avoid a canister and external pipes on a small tank.
bestFor: A tidy desktop nano where you do not want tubing or a canister on show.
highlights: 30 x 30 x 30 cm with about 21 L of display water
Rear filter chamber holds about 5.7 L
White background panel hides the equipment
Outflow nozzle included; pump and media are separate
watchOut: The pump is not included (UNS suggests the Sigma 5), and the chamber leaves less room for media than a canister would.

name: Limited Edition Rimless Aquarium
summary: Four popular UNS sizes with a frosted blue back panel and a heat-fused white bottom. The dimensions and build match the standard tanks; the difference is a built-in backdrop that makes plants and fish stand out without adding a separate background.
bestFor: Someone who wants a clean backdrop without fitting a film or light panel behind the tank.
highlights: Same glass thickness and sizes as the regular UNS range
watchOut: The backdrop is permanent, and the white base will show through anywhere the substrate is thin.

name: Prism Glass Tank with Flush Lid
summary: Tall rimless cubes that come with a mitred glass lid sitting flush with the top. The lid has a vent hole and grips, and it cuts evaporation and keeps jumpy fish in.
bestFor: Small cube aquariums where you want a lid that disappears, such as a betta, shrimp or specimen-plant nano.
highlights: Three sizes: 20TM, 25TM and 30TM (about 12 L to 37 L)
Flush-fitting glass lid with a central vent hole included
5 mm glass with a stabilising foam mat included

specs.Lid: Flush mitred glass lid with vent hole and grips

watchOut: The lid traps heat and moisture, so keep an eye on condensation and temperature under a strong light.

name: Rimless Cube Aquarium
summary: Equal sides on every face, from a tiny 16 cm cube up to a 60 cm cube that holds over 200 litres. Cubes pull the eye to the centre of the layout, so they work well for a single strong focal point or a row of matching tanks.
bestFor: Betta and shrimp tanks, centre-focused layouts, or a gallery of small cubes side by side.
highlights: Eight sizes from 16C (about 4 L) to 60C (about 216 L)
Glass steps up from 5 mm to 10 mm on the bigger sizes
45 degree mitred corners on low-iron glass
watchOut: Cubes are deep for their width, so the larger ones need a strong light to reach the substrate and long tools to reach the back.

name: Rimless Long Aquarium
summary: Long, narrow tanks that trade depth for a panoramic view. They give schooling nano fish a good run of open water and suit layouts that flow from one end to the other.
bestFor: Sideboard or shelf setups and river-style layouts built for a shoal of small fish.
highlights: Four sizes: 45L, 60L, 90B and 90L (about 13 L to 81 L)
Narrow depth keeps them shelf and sideboard friendly
Good swimming length for tetras and rasboras
watchOut: The shallow depth makes it harder to create a sense of perspective, so plan the layout carefully.

name: Rimless Nano Aquarium
summary: The 3N and 5N are the small UNS tanks a lot of people start with. They are low-iron rimless boxes with mitred corners, sized for a desk or shelf, and the 5N in particular has become a standard nano size that plenty of lights and filters are built around.
bestFor: A first planted nano, a shrimp colony or a desk scape where you want a clean glass box without a rim.
highlights: 5 mm low-iron glass with 45 degree mitred corners
Proportions suit a shrimp tank, betta tank or a small iwagumi
watchOut: Small water volumes swing fast in temperature and parameters, so dose and top up with care.

name: Rimless Shallow Aquarium
summary: Low-profile tanks that put the focus on rockwork, carpets and negative space. Light reaches the substrate easily and top-down viewing becomes part of the display.
bestFor: Iwagumi, carpet-heavy layouts and open-top scapes viewed from above as well as the front.
highlights: Eleven sizes from 16S (about 2 L) up to 120S (about 259 L)
SS models at 90 and 120 cm are extra shallow (25 cm tall)
Low height means carpets need less light and are easy to reach
5 mm to 12 mm glass depending on size
watchOut: Less water column means less room for tall stems and fewer fish, and evaporation shows quickly.

name: Rimless Standard Aquarium
summary: The core UNS range, running from the 45U through the very popular 60U up to a 180 cm show tank. These are classic rectangular proportions for a full foreground to background layout, with glass thickness that scales properly as the tanks get bigger.
bestFor: Nature-style and Dutch layouts where you want room for a proper foreground, midground and background.
highlights: Ten sizes from 45U (about 35 L) to 180U (about 648 L)
60U (60 x 36 x 36 cm, about 78 L) is the go-to mid-size planted tank
Glass from 5 mm up to 15 mm on the largest models
P, U and M suffixes give different depth and height options at 90 and 120 cm
Matching UNS stands exist for most sizes
watchOut: From 75P upwards these are heavy tanks, so plan the stand and floor loading before you buy.

name: Rimless Tall Aquarium
summary: Taller versions of the familiar UNS footprints, built for vertical layouts. Extra height gives stem plants room to grow and lets branches or rock reach up and out of the water.
bestFor: Jungle or forest-style layouts, tall stem plants and hardscape that breaks the surface.
highlights: Eight sizes from 16T (about 6 L) to 60T (about 97 L)
Same footprints as the cube, nano and standard tanks, just taller
watchOut: Height costs light at the substrate, so pair the taller models with a stronger fixture or low-light plants at the bottom.
